# Calculate p-value for nested F-test
# F-statistic = 3.2772
# Degrees of freedom: df1 = 2, df2 = 65

f_stat <- 3.2772
df1 <- 2  # numerator degrees of freedom (additional variables)
df2 <- 65 # denominator degrees of freedom (residual df from full model)

# Calculate p-value (upper tail probability)
p_value <- pf(f_stat, df1, df2, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Display result
p_value

# Importing required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Importing the dataset
ames_data <- read.csv("ames_housing_data.csv")
(head(ames_data))

# Dropping rows per EDA in Assignment 1
cat("Original data has:", nrow(ames_data), "rows\n")
ames_data_clean <- ames_data[ames_data$SaleCondition == "Normal" & 
                              ames_data$BldgType == "1Fam", ]
cat("Cleaned data has:", nrow(ames_data_clean), "rows\n")

# Fill missing values with 0
ames_data_clean[is.na(ames_data_clean)] <- 0

# Model 3: Quality/Age Variables
model3 <- lm(SalePrice ~ OverallQual + YearBuilt + YearRemodel + GarageYrBlt, data = ames_data_clean)

# Summary for individual coefficient tests and overall F-test
options(digits = 8)
summary(model3)
